summary: **For Petitioner** : Ms. Swapana Seshadri, Advocate, PGCIL Ms. Sneha Singh, Advocate, PGCIL Shri Utkarsh Singh, Advocate, PGCIL Shri Zafrul Hassan, PGCIL Shri Vishal Sagar, PGCIL Shri Mohd. Mohsin, PGCIL - _“1) Admit the capital cost as claimed in the Petition and approve the Additional Capitalisation incurred/projected to be incurred._ - _3) Condone the delay in commissioning of above mentioned assets as the reasons mentioned at para 6 are beyond the control of petitioner and allow IDC and IEDC as claimed in the petition._ - _4) Allow the Petitioner to recover the shortfall or refund the excess Annual Fixed Charges, on account of Return on Equity due to change in applicable Minimum Alternate/Corporate Income Tax rate as per the Income Tax Act, 1961 (as amended from time to time) of the respective financial year directly without making any application before the Commission as provided in Tariff Regulation 2019 as per para 8 above for respective block._ - _9) Allow the petitioner to claim the capital spares at the end of tariff block as per actual._ _and pass such other relief as Hon’ble Commission deems fit and appropriate under the circumstances of the case and in the interest of justice.”_ 5. The Petitioner has served the petition on the Respondents, and notice of this petition has been published in the newspaper in accordance with Section 64 of the Electricity Act, 2003. No comments or suggestions have been received from the general public in response to the aforesaid notice published in the newspaper by the Petitioner. Respondents and the clarifications given by the Petitioner are considered in the relevant portion of this order. 8. Having heard the representatives of the Petitioner and the Respondents, considering the submission of the Respondents and having perused the material on record, we proceed to dispose of the petition. conclusion in the order dated 11.10.2017 in Petition No. 187/MP/2015 that there is no negligence on the part of the Petitioner. 44. MPPMCL in its written submission has submitted that the reasons stated by the Petitioner for RoW claims are mainly confined to the obstruction/ resistance from the landowners and request made by the Petitioner for intervention/ assistance of the Government Authorities in dealing with them, which cannot be considered for condonation as these are routine in nature and Petitioner with an experience of 52. MPPMCL has submitted that the Petitioner attributed the delay to RoW issues such as obstruction/resistance from landowners and the need for Government intervention, which are routine challenges and cannot be grounds for condonation, particularly for the Petitioner, which has rich experience in executing transmission lines. In this regard, referring to the Commission’s order dated 23.6.2023 in Petition No. 470/MP/2019, has submitted that such issues do not constitute _force majeure_ unless accompanied by delays due to court stays/injunctions and legal proceedings, which must be examined separately. Therefore, the delay is attributable to the Petitioner and should not be condoned. 54. We have gone through the submissions of the Petitioner, MPPMCL and MSEDCL. The main contention of the respondents, i.e., MPPMCL and MSEDCL, is that the delay due to RoW issues is routine and cannot be considered under the _force majeure_ events. The Respondents also referred to the Commission’s order dated 23.6.2023 in Petition No. 470/MP/2019, wherein it was held that the RoW challenges must be anticipated by the licensee. The relevant portion of the Commission’s order dated 23.6.2023 in Petition No. 470/MP/2019 is as follows: _"47. In other words, whether the RoW issue, in particular case, qualifies as a force majeure event or not has to be examined on the basis of the facts & circumstances involved in each case and also the efforts & remedies availed by the licensee to resolve such issues in such case. As already noted above, the Petitioner has submitted the details of correspondences exchanged with various Authorities along with supporting documents. Insofar as they relate to the obstruction/ resistance from the land owners, request for intervention/ assistance of the Govt. Authorities in dealing with them etc. cannot be considered as force majeure event and no relief under force majeure can flow to the Petitioner as such activities are required to be anticipated by the licensee during the course of implementing the projects. However, what have to be distinguished from these generic efforts of resolving the RoW issues are the delays - owing to the stays/ injunctions granted by the Courts and the Court proceedings arising out these RoW issues & in the course of the Petitioner having availed the legal remedies in resolving the RoW issues. Accordingly, the delays attributable to the above aspect have been dealt with separately."_ 57. It is observed that the Petitioner has intermingled the details relating to payment of compensation with the RoW issues faced during the construction of the transmission line. From the documents placed on record, it is not possible to clearly ascertain the specific locations affected by RoW issues, how long they persisted, the date of 92. The Petitioner has sought reimbursement of the fee paid by it for filing the petition and the publication expenses. The Petitioner shall be entitled to reimbursement of the filing fees and publication expenses in connection with the present petition, directly from the beneficiaries on a pro-rata basis in accordance with Regulation 70(1) of the 2019 Tariff Regulations. 104.
